human_tolerance.notes: Uses wooded wetlands, ponds, lakes, rivers and streams with nearby tree cavities; values are authored estimates.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: US-wide authored envelope: nesting can start in late January in the South, early March in the Midwest, and March-April in the North; breeding can extend into July. Local timing varies.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Post-breeding molt and winter flocking; the broad phase is a simulation calendar, not a population-specific migration schedule.

sources.note: Conditions of Use confirms text CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Last resort for typical lifespan, explicit diurnality, locomotion (walking, flying, swimming), and social flocking/behavior details only. Alternatives checked 2026-11-01: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) supplies perching, dabbling, breeding and range but does not state diurnality or the full locomotion/social details; Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation reports a four-year wild average but its page provides no reuse licence; UF/IFAS and Missouri Extension repeat short-life claims under CC BY-NC-ND or other restrictive terms, rejected by project policy. ADW's narrative says 3-4 years and is the sole permissively allowed source found for that typical-life wording; its separate 270-month Bird Banding Laboratory row is internally conflicting and is excluded from the value. Wikipedia is a share-alike alternative for seeds, berries, insects, perching, breeding, and range, but does not mention aquatic plants or directly state day activity, walking/swimming, and evening flocking; ADW is retained for those exact claims only. There is no supported permissively licensed quantitative diet split, so proportions are authored rather than copied.

taxonomy.note: GBIF species match returned accepted Aix sponsa at species rank, usageKey 2498387; iNaturalist taxon 7107 is active and rank species.

external.note: Provider records checked 2026-11-01; GBIF match EXACT/ACCEPTED, iNaturalist active species; no synonym relationship reported.

range.note: North American native range; issue requests US curve. Introduced European records are excluded because the page describes captive escapees and no self-sustaining population.

traits.mass_kg.note: 0.600 kg is the midpoint of 454-862 g adult weight, converted from grams to kilograms.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Reported 454-862 g range converted to kg.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of reported 47-54 cm adult length, converted to metres.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of reported 66-73 cm wingspan, converted to metres.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Narrative in ADW Lifespan/Longevity gives average wild life as three or four years, distinct from roughly 15-year wild maximum. The same page has a conflicting Bird Banding Laboratory row labeled average 270 months; it is not used because it conflicts with the explicit typical-life narrative. The 3.5-year value is the midpoint of the stated 3-4-year range.

traits.diet.note: Modelled allocation of listed seeds/acorns, berries, insects, and aquatic plants. Fractions are authored, not measured diet percentages.

traits.social.note: Pairs and small flocks are described; group size bounds are a broad authored encoding.

traits.activity_pattern.note: ADW Behavior explicitly identifies the species as diurnal.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: flee to avoid predators; no measured defense tendency is asserted.

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement; no quantitative wariness evidence found.

habitat.use.note: Authored time allocation across aquatic/shore/tree/aerial strata from ADW habitat descriptions of freshwater wetlands and tree cavities.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Wooded wetlands and sleeping on water; pond is the nearest available shelter tag.

habitat.resources.note: Food tags represent listed seeds, berries, insects, and aquatic plants; pond, water, cavity and perch encode wetland use and nesting.

habitat.requires.note: Freshwater wetland habitat and cavity sites within one mile of water; 500 m requirement is an approximate authored distance.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Numeric tolerance values and Tolerant category are authored simulation judgements; no quantitative source found.

seasonal.strategy.note: Distribution describes northern populations migrating south and southern populations resident.

seasonal.phases.note: January-July is an authored US-wide nesting envelope from US Forest Service regional start dates and a July northern end; post-breeding flocking is a broad simulation calendar, not a population-specific migration schedule.

activity.US.note: Mean of the iNaturalist and GBIF normalized monthly shares for the United States. Both CC0/CC BY tier A queries are usable: 10,556 iNaturalist observations at place 1 and 5,427,005 GBIF occurrences for country US; all 12 monthly bins are populated. Observation frequency is a proxy for activity.

behavior.note: Species-local authored FSM for documented daytime dabbling in aquatic plants/invertebrates, shoreline seed/fruit feeding, walking, swimming, perching, flight escape, night rest, and US-wide January-July nesting. The broad nesting window combines regional reports; it omits courtship, brood care, and seasonal routing.

look.note: Adult male iridescent green/blue/plumage and chestnut body with female muted brown/gray plumage generalized to one stylized palette; proportions are judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Precocial ducklings leave the nest the day after hatching; juvenile duration/scale are authored approximations.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Authored neutral estimate because the source distinguishes resident southern birds from migrating northern populations but supplies no US-wide population share.

traits.limb_count.note: Bird anatomy; schema counts walking limbs and excludes wings.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: ADW Behavior states walking, flying, and swimming.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Authored Endotherm classification for a bird.

traits.flight.note: Powered flight is represented from the documented flying behavior.

traits.respiration.note: Authored lung-breathing classification for a bird.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Authored absence of metamorphosis for a bird.

traits.nest_type.note: Distribution/reproduction section: nests in tree cavities and nest boxes.

traits.perching.note: Described as a perching duck with claws adapted to perch in trees.

traits.size_class.note: Small class judgement from adult mass of 454-862 g.
